_comment: The repository settings a repository on these standards is expected to have.
Applied by scripts/apply-settings.sh, which reads before it writes and
previews by default. Every value here is required by something documented:
the reason is on the line beside it, and a setting nothing needs is not here.
SETTINGS ONLY. Branch and tag protection live in data/rulesets/ and are
applied separately, because they are the change that can lock you out.
Three endpoint groups, one plan: the repository block is the repository
object, the actions block is the Actions policy under Settings → Actions →
General (workflow token and fork pull requests), and the security block
Everything writable that is deliberately NOT here is in _excluded, with
the reason - absence is always a decision, never an oversight.
Some settings are gated on repository visibility or plan. Secret scanning is
free on public repositories and needs Advanced Security on private ones, and
private vulnerability reporting is a public-repository feature. The script
detects both and skips with a notice rather than failing the run.

_why.allow_squash_merge: Squash is the only door. The rulesets set allowed_merge_methods to squash on every protected branch; this makes the button agree.
_why.allow_merge_commit: A merge commit has no Conventional Commit subject, so the changelog generator cannot see it.
_why.allow_rebase_merge: Rebase replays commits individually, which puts unsquashed work-in-progress subjects on a protected branch.
_why.squash_merge_commit_title: The pull request title becomes the commit that lands, which is exactly what semantic-pr.yml validates.
_why.squash_merge_commit_message: The pull request body becomes the commit body, which is how the required commit body arrives without retyping it.
_why.delete_branch_on_merge: Documented in Repository-Hygiene as the on-merge cadence. Nothing else prunes merged heads.
_why.allow_auto_merge: REQUIRED, not cosmetic. dependabot-automerge.yml and open-pr.sh both call `gh pr merge --auto`, which fails without it.
_why.allow_update_branch: Lets a pull request take the base branch without a merge commit, so strict required checks can be satisfied.
_why.web_commit_signoff_required: The DCO check requires a Signed-off-by trailer on every human commit; this makes edits made in the browser comply instead of failing.
_why.has_issues: The issue forms, the label taxonomy, and the intake chooser are all fronted by Issues. It is on by default everywhere; this puts it back if it was ever turned off.
_why.has_discussions: SUPPORT.md and the issue chooser route questions to Discussions, and the chooser's link 404s until this is on. The public template ships the discussion forms it expects.
_why.has_wiki: Documentation is versioned in the tree and reviewed. A wiki is neither.
_why.has_projects: Off by default rather than opinionated: turn it on deliberately if you use it.

_why_actions.default_workflow_permissions: Branch-Protection says to leave Workflow permissions on Read and write, and means it: every stub declares its own permissions ceiling and this setting caps them all. On read-only, a called workflow asking for issues: write fails before any job starts, with no log to read.
_why_actions.can_approve_pull_request_reviews: open-pr.sh opens pull requests as github-actions and dependabot-automerge.yml approves them; both are refused without this and can only tell you to come flip it by hand.
_why_actions.fork_pr_approval_policy: Every first-time contributor's fork workflows wait for a maintainer, whether or not the account is new to GitHub. This is the floor: raise it to all_external_contributors in a settings-file override where the repository handles anything sensitive. PUBLIC repositories only - GitHub refuses the endpoint on a private repository, which an outsider cannot fork, so the run skips it with a notice.

_excluded._comment: Every writable repository setting that is deliberately NOT here, so absence is always a decision and never an oversight. The complete map, including what generation sets and what has no API at all, is docs/operations/Repository-Settings.md.
_excluded.name, description, homepage, topics: Identity. Initialisation rewrites what the template stamped; what the project is called and about is yours, and a shared value would overwrite it on every run.
_excluded.private / visibility: Changing who can see a repository is a human act with legal and billing consequences, never a side effect of a settings sync.
_excluded.archived, is_template, default_branch: Structural state. Generation inherits the default branch (Development) from the template; archiving and templating are one-time decisions.
_excluded.advanced_security / code_security: Paid per-committer on private repositories. Billing decisions belong to a person, so the script only uses security features where they are already available.
_excluded.secret_scanning_ai_detection: Copilot secret scanning is plan-gated and still moving; turn it on by hand where your plan has it.
_excluded.merge_commit_title, merge_commit_message: They configure a door this standard nails shut: allow_merge_commit is false, so no one could ever see these values.
_excluded.allow_forking: Exists only on organization-owned repositories; personal public repositories are always forkable.
_excluded.actions enabled / allowed_actions allowl: Actions is tautologically on - this workflow ran on it. An action allowlist is real hardening with a real maintenance bill (every newly pinned action needs the list edited), and the standards already pin actions by commit SHA, which an allowlist does not improve on. Restrict deliberately under Settings → Actions → General if you want it.
_excluded.actions workflow access_level: Governs private repositories sharing workflows outward; these standards publish shared workflows from one public repository instead.
_excluded.environments: Protection rules name human reviewers, which no shared file can know. The manual-hardening list in docs/operations/Repository-Settings.md covers setting them up.
_excluded.pages, webhooks, autolinks, deploy keys,: Project-specific wiring with no standard value.
_excluded.interaction_limits: Temporary moderation levers by design; a sync that re-applied them would turn an incident response into permanent policy.

_why_security.secret_scanning: Security-&-Secrets names it as the platform-native layer beside Gitleaks.
_why_security.secret_scanning_push_protection: Stops a credential at the boundary rather than reporting it afterwards.
_why_security.secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns: Widens platform scanning past provider tokens to generic credentials - private keys, connection strings - the same class Gitleaks hunts from the other side. Plan-gated: written only where the repository reports the feature, skipped with a notice everywhere else.
_why_security.vulnerability_alerts: Dependabot alerts. The dependency-management standard assumes they are on.
_why_security.automated_security_fixes: Dependabot security updates, which is what opens the pull requests that dependabot-automerge.yml then handles.
_why_security.private_vulnerability_reporting: Gives the Security tab a Report a vulnerability entry, which is the intake SECURITY.md points at.
